newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Izetbegovic calls for NATO general to leave.
newsitem.headline: Izetbegovic calls for NATO general to leave.

text.p: An angry Bosnian President called on Friday for NATO Lieutenant-General Sir Michael Walker, who commands NATO-led ground forces in Bosnia, to leave the country.

Speaking in an interview on government television, Alija Izetbegovic criticized NATO forces for overreacting to fighting which broke out between Moslems and Serbs around the village of Gajevi in Tuesday.
NATO blamed the Bosnian government and its army for provoking the fighting by encouraging a group of refugees to try to return to their homes in Serb-held Gajevi without prior international approval.

In response, NATO raided a Bosnian army brigade headquarters near Gajevi on Thursday and confiscated hundreds of Kalashnikov assault rifles and tonnes of munitions. It later began destroying the material.
The Bosnian president also expressed unhappiness about NATO troops who held Bosnian army commander General Rasim Delic at a checkpoint west of Sarajevo on Thursday for 45 minutes.
Izetbegovic referred to "imprudent and politically immature" actions by NATO in the television interview and said: "We will demand the replacement of General Walker, who ordered these actions."
Walker is the British commander of NATO's ACE Rapid Reaction Corps, which forms the nucleus of international ground forces in Bosnia.
He is already scheduled to return to Germany next week in a long-planned rotation of duties.
